questions.q: Which word serves as a minimal pair for the word 'fat' to contrast the `/f/` and `/v/` consonant sounds?
questions.explain: A minimal pair differs by only one phonological element. 'Fat' (`/fæt/`) and 'vat' (`/væt/`) contrast the unvoiced `/f/` and voiced `/v/` sounds.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Identify the minimal pair that contrasts the consonants `/p/` and `/b/` from the base word 'pin'.
questions.explain: 'Pin' (`/pɪn/`) and 'bin' (`/bɪn/`) form a minimal pair highlighting the unvoiced `/p/` and voiced `/b/` plosive sounds.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which of the following pairs is a minimal pair contrasting `/s/` and `/z/`?
questions.explain: The words 'sip' (`/sɪp/`) and 'zip' (`/zɪp/`) differ only in the initial consonant, perfectly contrasting the voiceless `/s/` and voiced `/z/`.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Identify the minimal pair that contrasts the consonants `/k/` and `/g/`.
questions.explain: The words 'coat' (`/kəʊt/`) and 'goat' (`/gəʊt/`) are identical except for their initial unvoiced `/k/` and voiced `/g/` consonant sounds.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Identify the minimal pair that properly contrasts the alveolar plosives `/t/` and `/d/`.
questions.explain: The words 'tip' and 'dip' differ only in the initial consonants `/t/` (voiceless) and `/d/` (voiced), making them a minimal pair for these sounds.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which of the following creates a minimal pair contrasting `/f/` and `/v/`?
questions.explain: The words 'fan' and 'van' contrast the unvoiced labiodental fricative `/f/` and its voiced counterpart `/v/`.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Identify the minimal pair contrasting `/s/` and `/z/`.
questions.explain: Both 'rice' (`/s/`) vs 'rise' (`/z/`) and 'sink' (`/s/`) vs 'zinc' (`/z/`) form valid minimal pairs contrasting the unvoiced `/s/` and voiced `/z/` sounds.
questions.exam: BECE English Studies: Spoken English & Oral
questions.subject: English Studies

questions.q: Which pair of words forms a minimal pair contrasting `/p/` and `/b/`?
questions.explain: All options demonstrate the `/p/` and `/b/` contrast. 'Rope'/'robe' (final), 'pit'/'bit' (initial), and 'cap'/'cab' (final) differ only by the unvoiced/voiced bilabial plosive.
